title: Build Execution into Strategy
coreMove: Earn cooperation by engaging people before the choice, explaining the reasoning after it, and making the new expectations unmistakable.
sourcePressure: Use fair process: engagement, explanation, and expectation clarity, so execution commitment is built during strategy formation rather than demanded afterward.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Thinking fair process means consensus, endless input, or making everyone happy with the final decision.

sourceAnchors.name: fair process
sourceAnchors.detail: official support defines fair process around engagement, explanation, and expectation clarity
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Fair process has three plain tests: people were engaged, the decision was explained, and the expectations are clear enough to act on.

hook: Do not open with a competitor scoreboard, a war metaphor, or a generic market map.
Do not use A crowded market is not..., The real strategy is..., or What if growth... as reusable shells.
counterintuition: Avoid Most people assume... but actually... and The opposite is true.
Avoid turning every chapter into competition bad, creativity good.
tryThisNow: Avoid Set a timer for 60 seconds and list... as a repeated action.
Avoid generic reflect on your strategy prompts.
examples: Avoid conference-room whiteboard workshops as the default scene.
Avoid repeating mugs, markers, dosing cups, bike helmets, radiators, bus depots, classrooms, narrow kitchens, or generic dashboard scenes.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: delivery route redesign and driver engagement
exampleSpecs.audience: a dispatch leader under pressure to cut fuel
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether drivers follow the new route or quietly route around it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she sees public agreement turn into private workarounds because driver knowledge was never engaged
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The locked route map glows above the dispatch counter while three drivers compare detours

exampleSpecs.domain: software architecture decision with explanation and build rules
exampleSpecs.audience: a technical lead choosing under deadline pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether engineers commit to a decision they did not all prefer
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he must choose one architecture after engaging risks, then explain the tradeoff and write build rules clearly
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You can hear the server fans while Etienne watches two senior engineers wait for the call

exampleSpecs.domain: clinic digital check-in shaped by staff and patient trials
exampleSpecs.audience: a healthcare leader replacing paper forms
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether staff and patients cooperate with a required change
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: engagement changes implementation details without reversing the decision to replace paper
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Anders one lobby trial to learn the tablet stand was facing the wrong people

exampleSpecs.domain: retail uniform change tied to service expectations
exampleSpecs.audience: a store manager rolling out a customer-visibility strategy
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether staff see the change as branding whim or service logic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she gives the reason and exact new behavior instead of issuing only the uniform rule
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Are we mannequins now?" a cashier asks Lin, tugging the blue vest from its sleeve

exampleSpecs.domain: childcare staffing schedule and fake engagement
exampleSpecs.audience: a center director balancing ratios, parents, and staff fatigue
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether staff follow the schedule or trade shifts unofficially
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he sees that fake engagement damaged trust more than a direct decision would have
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 6:05 p.m., Ryan finds three unofficial shift swaps taped inside a cubby door

exampleSpecs.domain: theater stage plot and unclear expectations
exampleSpecs.audience: a production lead trying to speed scene changes
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether crew cooperation survives opening week
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she predicts a walkthrough created buy-in, then missed cues reveal expectations were never clear
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Gaffer tape peels up at center stage as Catarina hears the wrong flat roll in

skillTargets: apply engagement, explanation, and expectation clarity
predict execution failure when people were bypassed

tryThisNowSpec: For one decision people must execute, write the engagement you owe, the reason you will explain, and the exact expectation.
